title: The Last Choir Again
premise: August Okafor, junior ledger-keeper of the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers that the guild's oldest account—a debt owed to the last dragon—has come due just as the old gods resume answering prayers. When she learns the gods' return is fueled by stolen dragon-fire, and that her own bloodline was the price of the original bargain, August must choose between exposing the guild's founding crime and letting the last dragon die in silence. In the end, she burns the ledgers, offers her secret to the dragon instead of the war, and forges a ragged found family from debtors, defrocked priests, and one very old serpent—paying for survival with everything she thought kept her safe.
about_author: Jude Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing debts, wills, and confessions before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep records of things everyone else would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Numbers
chapters.summary: August's POV. She balances the guild's books on the eve of the Ember Audit, hiding her own name in the margins where no one looks. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Nine Members, One Chair
chapters.summary: The guild meets; only six attend. Master Corvane assigns August to audit the sealed vault as a test no one expects her to pass. Beat: being underestimated as both shield and wound.

chapters.title: What the Vault Keeps
chapters.summary: August finds an account older than the guild itself: a debt of fire owed to something called Vaskarath. Her hands shake over the entry. Beat: first crack in the world she trusted.

chapters.title: Prayers with Return Addresses
chapters.summary: Priest-turned-debtor Sefa arrives claiming the gods answered her prayer for rain—in a city with no clouds left. August logs it as impossible. Beat: wonder edged with dread.

chapters.title: The Ledger That Reads Back
chapters.summary: August's POV. The old account begins writing entries she never made, in handwriting like her own. Beat: the past reaching through paper to claim her.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Corvane shows unexpected warmth, teaching August the guild's true trade: not miracles, but the management of what people owe. Beat: mentorship laced with manipulation.

chapters.title: Smoke Without Fire
chapters.summary: Sefa and August trace answered prayers across the city; each miracle leaves a cold ash that matches nothing in any ledger. Beat: detective intimacy, friendship kindling.

chapters.title: Vaskarath
chapters.summary: August reads the founding contract aloud: the guild bought its survival with dragon-fire, and someone's bloodline guaranteed it. The signature is her grandmother's. Beat: identity detonation.

chapters.title: Running the Numbers
chapters.summary: August calculates how much fire remains—and how many prayers the gods can buy before it gutters out. Beat: horror of arithmetic, survival as accounting.

chapters.title: The Debtor's Choir
chapters.summary: A chorus of guild debtors gathers, each owing one impossible thing. August realizes they are her only allies. Beat: found family assembling by accident.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Corvane questions August about the missing page; she lies for the first time in her life. Beat: guilt and exhilaration of deception.

chapters.title: Down Where the Ash Falls Up
chapters.summary: Following the cold ash, August and Sefa descend into the undercity and find a shrine built around a dying flame. Beat: awe curdling into grief.

chapters.title: The Serpent Under the City
chapters.summary: Vaskarath speaks—not a monster but an exhausted ancient, showing August the theft of her grandmother's generation. Beat: sympathy for the supposed beast.

chapters.title: Terms of the Original Sin
chapters.summary: Vaskarath explains: the gods feed on dragon-fire; when it ends, they end—or they take it back by war. Beat: the stakes made explicit and terrible.

chapters.title: August Makes a Withdrawal
chapters.summary: She secretly moves funds from guild accounts to fund her investigation, forging entries flawlessly. Beat: becoming what the ledgers always feared.

chapters.title: Sefa's Second Prayer
chapters.summary: Sefa prays again, testing whether the gods know her name now. Something answers with her dead brother's voice. Beat: temptation wearing love's face.

chapters.title: The Audit Arrives Early
chapters.summary: External auditors from the Concord of Faiths arrive; the guild must produce every account, including the sealed one. Beat: clock starts ticking loudly.

chapters.title: Forgery as Love Language
chapters.summary: August teaches the debtor-choir to forge, hide, and lie—corrupting them gently to protect them. Beat: moral erosion framed as care.

chapters.title: Corvane Knew
chapters.summary: August confronts Corvane; he admits he's known about her bloodline since her hiring. She was inventory, not family. Beat: betrayal at the heart of belonging.

chapters.title: The Gods Send a Bill
chapters.summary: A divine emissary demands the guild surrender 'the guarantor'—August—to settle the fire-debt peacefully. Beat: being priced, literally.

chapters.title: Vote of Nine
chapters.summary: The guild votes on handing her over. Three vote no; four yes; two abstain. August watches her worth counted in raised hands. Beat: institutional cruelty, intimate devastation.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Ledger Halls
chapters.summary: August flees with the founding contract; the choir covers her escape with staged fires and forged trails. Beat: loyalty proven in action.

chapters.title: What Sefa Chose
chapters.summary: Sefa reveals she reported August's location to hear her brother again—then burned the message and chose August instead. Beat: forgiveness tested and granted.

chapters.title: The Cold Cathedral
chapters.summary: Hiding in the abandoned cathedral of a god who died first, August finds records proving gods can starve quietly rather than wage war. Beat: hope with a terrible cost.

chapters.title: Negotiating With Hunger
chapters.summary: August proposes a third path: rationed fire, freely given, so gods fade gently instead of fighting. Vaskarath laughs—no one has ever offered him a choice. Beat: audacity of compassion.

chapters.title: The Concord Closes In
chapters.summary: Auditors and divine agents surround the undercity; the choir's forgeries begin failing under scrutiny. Beat: net tightening, panic rising.

chapters.title: Price of a Name
chapters.summary: August learns surrendering her bloodline wouldn't end it—the gods want the whole guild extinguished to erase the evidence. Beat: relief inverted into larger dread.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Cornered, Corvane reveals he voted yes to save the guild, believing sacrifice was the guild's entire purpose. August rejects his arithmetic. Beat: antagonist humanized, ideology refuted.

chapters.title: The Ledger Burns Both Ways
chapters.summary: August realizes burning the founding contract voids the debt—but also dissolves the guild's charter and every protection it grants. Beat: the choice crystallized.

chapters.title: Choir Practice
chapters.summary: The debtors choose to stand with her, each paying their 'impossible thing' toward the plan. Beat: found family fully formed, willing to burn.

chapters.title: The Ember Audit
chapters.summary: Climax begins: before the Concord, August opens the sealed account publicly and reads the guild's founding crime aloud. Beat: truth as weapon.

chapters.title: Fire Answers
chapters.summary: Vaskarath rises beneath the city; the gods manifest to claim their fuel; the square becomes a battlefield of light and ash. Beat: chaos, spectacle, terror.

chapters.title: August's Entry
chapters.summary: She writes herself into the ledger as sole debtor, offering her bloodline's fire willingly—if the gods accept rations instead of war. Beat: self-sacrifice as negotiation.

chapters.title: What the Gods Cannot Refuse
chapters.summary: The starving gods, shown the cold cathedral's precedent, waver. The eldest accepts the ration; the youngest refuses and attacks. Beat: schism among the divine.

chapters.title: Guttering
chapters.summary: In the battle, Vaskarath shields the choir and begins to fail; Sefa spends her brother's voice—one final prayer—to call rain of real water. Beat: costly grace.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: August burns the founding contract mid-battle; the debt dies, the guild charter dissolves, and the gods' claim evaporates with it. Beat: liberation through destruction.

chapters.title: Ashes, Counted
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the guild is dissolved, Corvane resigns into obscurity, and the surviving members gather in the ruined hall with no charter between them. Beat: loss and strange freedom.

chapters.title: A New Kind of Account
chapters.summary: The choir reforms as something unchartered—a cooperative that gives fire, records kindnesses, and owes nothing to anyone. Beat: rebuilding on chosen bonds.

chapters.title: Vaskarath's Morning
chapters.summary: August visits the dragon, now fed by voluntary offerings; he tells her her grandmother would have wanted the ledgers burned long ago. Beat: reconciliation with inheritance.

chapters.title: The First Free Page
chapters.summary: Final chapter, August's POV. She opens a blank ledger, writes the choir's names—not as debtors but as signatories—and finally writes her own name large. Beat: belonging, claimed at last.
